questions.text: What is the mean of the data set: {4, 8, 6, 10, 12}?
What is the median of the data set: {15, 3, 8, 12, 7, 20, 9}?
questions.explanation: Order data from least to greatest: {3, 7, 8, 9, 12, 15, 20}. With 7 values, the middle value (4th position) is 9.

questions.text: What is the mode of the data set: {5, 2, 7, 5, 8, 2, 5, 9, 1}?
options: 5 and 2
questions.explanation: The mode is the most frequently occurring value. The number 5 appears three times, more than any other value.

questions.text: What is the range of the numbers: {14, 28, 5, 33, 19, 42}?
questions.explanation: Range = Maximum – Minimum = 42 – 5 = 37.

questions.text: A standard six-sided die is rolled once. What is the probability of rolling a prime number?
questions.explanation: The outcomes on a die are {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}. The prime numbers are {2, 3, 5} (3 outcomes). Probability = 3 / 6 = 1/2.

questions.text: A bag contains 4 red, 6 blue, and 5 green marbles. If one marble is drawn at random, what is the probability that it is NOT blue?
questions.explanation: Total marbles = 4 + 6 + 5 = 15. Marbles that are not blue = 4 (red) + 5 (green) = 9. Probability = 9 / 15 = 3/5.

questions.text: Two fair coins are flipped simultaneously. What is the probability of getting at least one head?
questions.explanation: Sample space = {HH, HT, TH, TT} (4 equally likely outcomes). Outcomes with at least one head = {HH, HT, TH} (3 outcomes). Probability = 3/4.

questions.text: A student scores 85, 90, and 88 on three tests. What score must the student earn on the fourth test to have an average of 90?
questions.explanation: Required total score for 4 tests = 4 · 90 = 360. Current sum = 85 + 90 + 88 = 263. Required fourth score = 360 – 263 = 97.

questions.text: How many different 4-digit PIN numbers can be formed using the digits 0–9 if digits CANNOT be repeated?
questions.explanation: By the fundamental counting principle (permutations): 10 · 9 · 8 · 7 = 5,040.

questions.text: How many ways can a committee of 3 students be chosen from a group of 8 candidates?
questions.explanation: Since order of selection does not matter, use combinations: ₈C₃ = 8! / (3! · 5!) = (8 · 7 · 6) / (3 · 2 · 1) = 56.

questions.text: If events A and B are independent, P(A) = 0.4, and P(B) = 0.5, what is P(A and B)?
questions.explanation: For independent events, P(A and B) = P(A) · P(B) = 0.4 · 0.5 = 0.20.

questions.text: If the standard deviation of a data set is 0, what can be concluded about the data values?
options: All values in the data set are identical
The mean of the data set is 0
The data set contains no values
The data is normally distributed
questions.explanation: Standard deviation measures dispersion. A standard deviation of 0 indicates zero variation, meaning every single value in the data set is identical to the mean.

questions.text: In a normal distribution, approximately what percentage of data falls within one standard deviation of the mean?
questions.explanation: According to the empirical rule (68-95-99.7 rule) for normal distributions, approximately 68% of the data falls within ±1 standard deviation of the mean.

questions.text: What is the median of the data set: {6, 10, 14, 18}?
questions.explanation: For an even number of ordered values, the median is the mean of the two middle values: (10 + 14) / 2 = 24 / 2 = 12.

questions.text: A card is drawn from a standard 52-card deck. What is the probability of drawing an Ace or a King?
questions.explanation: There are 4 Aces and 4 Kings (8 cards total) in a 52-card deck. P(Ace or King) = 8 / 52 = 2 / 13.

questions.text: A survey of 200 people found that 120 prefer coffee and 80 prefer tea. What is the probability that a randomly chosen person prefers tea?
How many different ways can 5 runners finish in 1st, 2nd, and 3rd place in a race?
questions.explanation: Order matters (permutations): ₅P₃ = 5 · 4 · 3 = 60 ways.

questions.text: If a spinner has 8 equal sections numbered 1 through 8, what is the probability of landing on a number greater than 5?
questions.explanation: Numbers greater than 5 are {6, 7, 8} (3 outcomes out of 8). Probability = 3/8.

questions.text: A box plot shows a median of 45, lower quartile (Q1) of 30, and upper quartile (Q3) of 60. What is the interquartile range (IQR)?
questions.explanation: Interquartile Range IQR = Q3 – Q1 = 60 – 30 = 30.

questions.text: If the mean of 5 numbers is 14, what is their total sum?
questions.explanation: Since the arithmetic mean of a data set is defined as the total sum divided by the number of items (Mean = Sum / n), the total sum is calculated as: Sum = Mean · Count = 14 · 5 = 70.

questions.text:
Which underlined word maintains the most consistent formal tone in an academic research paper on ocean conservation?

'Marine reserves play a ______ role in protecting endangered biodiversity.'
options: crucial
super cool
gigantic
crazy
questions.explanation: 'Crucial' is a precise, elevated academic adjective, whereas 'super cool', 'gigantic', and 'crazy' are colloquial and inappropriate for scholarly writing.

questions.text: Which sentence would NOT be acceptable in an otherwise serious, objective biography of Abraham Lincoln?
options: Lincoln was a totally rad dude who handled politics with ease.
Lincoln navigated complex geopolitical and military challenges during the Civil War.
Lincoln issued the Emancipation Proclamation in January 1863.
His leadership style emphasized patience, strategic communication, and moral resolve.
questions.explanation: The phrase 'totally rad dude' is modern informal slang that violently clashes with the serious, objective tone of a historical biography.

questions.text:
Which of the following revisions best replaces the informal phrase in brackets?

'The laboratory technicians [threw together] the test results before the conference.'
options: compiled
slapped out
whipped up
tossed up
questions.explanation: 'Compiled' is a formal, professional verb that accurately describes the systematic assembly of scientific data.

questions.text: The author is writing an enthusiastic review of a classical symphony performance. Which choice best reflects this tone?
options: The orchestra delivered a breathtaking, masterfully nuanced performance that held the audience spellbound.
The orchestra played the notes written on the sheet music.
The concert was okay, I guess.
The instruments made sound vibrations for two hours.
questions.explanation: Vivid, elevated modifiers ('breathtaking', 'masterfully nuanced', 'held the audience spellbound') convey authentic artistic enthusiasm and critical appreciation.

questions.text:
Which word creates the most appropriate formal register in this sentence?

'The board of directors ______ the CEO's strategic proposal.'
options: endorsed
gave a thumbs up to
was hyped about
went crazy for
questions.explanation: 'Endorsed' is standard corporate and formal vocabulary for expressing institutional approval.

questions.text: Which option best maintains the somber, reflective tone of a passage describing an ancient cemetery at twilight?
options: Shadows lengthened across the moss-covered headstones as a solemn quiet settled over the valley.
The cemetery had lots of old rocks sticking out of the dirt.
Ghosts were probably hanging out around the tombstones.
It was getting dark and spooky around the dead people.
questions.explanation: Poetic imagery ('Shadows lengthened', 'moss-covered headstones', 'solemn quiet') establishes a respectful, atmospheric, and somber mood.

questions.text: In an informative article for young elementary students, which explanation of photosynthesis has the most suitable tone?
options: Plants use sunlight, water, and air to make their own food, like a little kitchen inside their green leaves!
Photosynthetic autotrophs undergo photophosphorylation within thylakoid membranes.
Plants eat dirt and sun.
Plants have complicated chemical reactions that you cannot understand yet.
questions.explanation: A warm, engaging analogy ('like a little kitchen') provides accessible, age-appropriate clarity without overly technical jargon or condescension.

questions.text: Which sentence displays an inappropriately dramatic tone for a standard weather report?
options: A monstrous, apocalyptic drizzle will descend from the heavens to drown our fragile hopes tomorrow morning.
Light rain is expected throughout the morning hours, tapering off by midday.
Temperatures will remain mild with scattered showers across the region.
Winds from the northwest will bring occasional light precipitation.
questions.explanation: Hyperbolic melodrama ('monstrous', 'apocalyptic', 'drown our fragile hopes') for a minor drizzle is an absurd tone violation for meteorology.

questions.text: Which choice provides the most objective and neutral description of a controversial political debate?
options: Both candidates presented contrasting perspectives on fiscal policy, citing different economic indicators to support their proposals.
One candidate crushed the other candidate with devastating insults.
The debate was a total waste of time with zero substance.
Both candidates were completely clueless about the economy.
questions.explanation: Choice A uses neutral, impartial analytical phrasing ('contrasting perspectives', 'citing different economic indicators') appropriate for objective journalism.

questions.text:
Which word best completes the sentence while maintaining a respectful, scholarly tone?

'Scholars ______ the poet's pioneering contributions to twentieth-century literature.'
options: commemorate
fanboy over
brag about
cheer on
questions.explanation: 'Commemorate' (or 'recognize') reflects formal literary scholarship, whereas 'fanboy over' and 'brag about' are informal colloquialisms.

questions.text:
Which revision best removes the pretentious, overly convoluted wording?

'It is incumbent upon our pedagogical facilitators to utilize innovative instructional modalities.'
options: Teachers should use creative teaching methods.
Pedagogical facilitators must execute instructional mechanisms.
It is a vital necessity for educator personnel to utilize modalities.
Facilitators of pedagogy ought to implement learning vectors.
questions.explanation: Choice A translates inflated, bureaucratic jargon ('pedagogical facilitators', 'instructional modalities') into clear, direct, natural English.

questions.text: Which option best maintains the urgent, cautionary tone of an environmental warning about melting glaciers?
options: Accelerating glacial retreat threatens coastal communities worldwide, demanding immediate and coordinated international action.
Glaciers are melting a little bit, which is kind of a bummer.
Ice turns into water when it gets hot outside.
Maybe someone should check on the polar ice caps sometime.
questions.explanation: Urgent diction ('Accelerating glacial retreat', 'threatens coastal communities', 'demanding immediate... action') conveys genuine gravity and importance.

questions.text:
Which phrase creates an inconsistent, informal tone in this formal lab report sentence?

'The compound was heated to 100°C, and then the mixture [went totally nuts] as gas bubbles formed.'
options: reacted vigorously
went totally nuts
showed a wild reaction
freaked out completely
questions.explanation: 'Reacted vigorously' is the proper scientific phrasing to replace the colloquial phrase 'went totally nuts'.

questions.text: The writer wants to describe an elegant ballroom dance. Which choice best creates an atmosphere of grace and sophistication?
options: Couples glided across the polished mahogany floor in seamless, synchronized harmony.
People stomped around the dance floor to the music.
A bunch of dancers moved back and forth in the room.
The dancers did their steps without crashing into each other.
questions.explanation: Elevated sensory descriptors ('glided', 'polished mahogany floor', 'seamless, synchronized harmony') create an atmosphere of refined elegance.

questions.text: Which choice best avoids biased, loaded language in a news report?
options: The mayor announced a new municipal budget proposal on Tuesday.
The stubborn mayor pushed his terrible budget on Tuesday.
The heroic mayor saved the city with his genius budget on Tuesday.
The reckless mayor schemed a sneaky budget on Tuesday.
questions.explanation: Choice A is purely factual and impartial, avoiding subjective or loaded adjectives ('stubborn', 'terrible', 'heroic', 'reckless').

questions.text:
Which underlined word is most appropriate for a formal legal brief?

'The defendant ______ that the contract was signed under duress.'
options: asserts
claims like crazy
yells
whines
questions.explanation: 'Asserts' is a standard formal legal term for making a formal claim in judicial pleadings.

questions.text: Which sentence establishes a humorous, self-deprecating tone in a personal essay?
options: My first attempt at baking sourdough resulted in a loaf so dense it could have served as a foundation stone for a medieval castle.
Sourdough bread is made using wild yeast and lactic acid bacteria.
I made a loaf of bread and it was bad.
The chemical reactions in my bread failed.
questions.explanation: The hyperbole ('foundation stone for a medieval castle') playfully mocks the narrator's own culinary failure with charming, self-deprecating humor.

questions.text:
Which phrase maintains an appropriate formal tone in an executive summary?

'The merger will significantly ______ operational efficiency across both divisions.'
options: enhance
amp up
boost big time
supercharge
questions.explanation: 'Enhance' is standard formal business vocabulary, whereas 'amp up', 'boost big time', and 'supercharge' are colloquial slang.

questions.text: Which option best reflects an admiring, appreciative tone toward an artist's craft?
options: Her intricate brushwork reflects decades of disciplined devotion to the mastery of light and shadow.
She painted paintings using a brush and oils.
Her paintings are okay if you like art.
She spent too much time messing with colors.
questions.explanation: Descriptive diction ('intricate brushwork', 'disciplined devotion', 'mastery') expresses deep admiration and appreciation for artistic skill.

questions.text: Which sentence maintains consistency of formal academic style throughout?
options: Researchers investigated the archaeological site using ground-penetrating radar to identify subterranean structures.
Researchers checked out the old ruins using radar to see cool buried stuff.
Scientists did research at the dig site and found a ton of artifacts.
Archaeologists scoped out the place with technology.
questions.explanation: Choice A utilizes formal, precise scientific and academic terminology ('investigated', 'archaeological site', 'ground-penetrating radar', 'subterranean structures').

questions.text:
Electric vehicles produce zero direct tailpipe emissions. ______, manufacturing their batteries requires significant energy and rare earth minerals.

Which transition word best connects these sentences?
options: However
Furthermore
Therefore
Similarly
questions.explanation: 'However' correctly establishes the contrast between the environmental benefit of zero emissions and the environmental cost of battery production.

questions.text:
The student studied diligently every evening for three months. ______, she achieved the highest score in the statewide competition.

Which transition best expresses this relationship?
options: Consequently
In contrast
Nevertheless
Otherwise
questions.explanation: 'Consequently' signals a direct cause-and-effect outcome: diligent studying led directly to the top test score.

questions.text:
The museum offers free admission on the first Sunday of every month. ______, it provides complimentary audio guides to all visitors.

Which transition word best adds information?
options: In addition
Instead
Conversely
On the other hand
questions.explanation: 'In addition' appropriately adds another complementary benefit (free audio guides) to the initial perk (free admission).

questions.text:
Heavy fog rolled into the valley, reducing visibility to less than fifty feet. ______, airport officials grounded all departing flights.

Which transition word is most logical?
options: As a result
Meanwhile
Nonetheless
Conversely
questions.explanation: Grounding the flights was the direct result of the dense fog, so the causal transition 'As a result' is logically necessary.

questions.text: Ancient Greek democracy allowed citizens to vote directly on legislation. Roman republicanism, ______, relied on elected representatives to govern.
options: in contrast
for instance
furthermore
likewise
questions.explanation: 'In contrast' highlights the fundamental structural difference between direct democracy (Greek) and representative republicanism (Roman).

questions.text:
The new library features thousands of print volumes. ______, it houses state-of-the-art digital media labs and study pods.

Which transition provides continuation?
options: Moreover
Despite this
Nevertheless
Regardless
questions.explanation: 'Moreover' adds an additional technological enhancement that complements the library's traditional book collection.

questions.text: The forecast called for clear skies all weekend. ______, an unexpected coastal squall dumped three inches of rain on the festival.
options: Nevertheless
Thus
In other words
Therefore
questions.explanation: 'Nevertheless' conveys a concession/contrast between the sunny forecast and the surprising torrential rain.

questions.text: The chef recommends using fresh herbs whenever possible. ______, dried herbs can be substituted if fresh ones are unavailable.
options: However
Therefore
In fact
Accordingly
questions.explanation: 'However' introduces the alternative concession that dried herbs can be used if the ideal choice (fresh herbs) is not on hand.

questions.text: Many nocturnal animals rely on senses other than sight. Bats, ______, navigate through echolocation.
options: for example
however
consequently
nevertheless
questions.explanation: 'For example' introduces bats as a specific, illustrative case of an animal using non-visual senses.

questions.text: Regular aerobic exercise strengthens the cardiovascular system. ______, it has been shown to reduce anxiety and elevate mood.
options: Additionally
On the contrary
Otherwise
Instead
questions.explanation: 'Additionally' introduces another distinct health benefit of exercise (mental/emotional health) alongside cardiovascular fitness.

questions.text: The company failed to innovate in response to digital technology. ______, it was forced to declare bankruptcy after eighty years in business.
options: Ultimately
Conversely
Meanwhile
In contrast
questions.explanation: 'Ultimately' denotes the final cumulative outcome of the company's long-term failure to innovate.

questions.text: A balanced diet provides essential vitamins and minerals. ______, it supplies the energy necessary for daily physical and cognitive activities.
options: Furthermore
Nevertheless
Even so
In contrast
questions.explanation: 'Furthermore' connects two additive benefits of maintaining a balanced diet.

questions.text: The experiment yielded inconclusive data during the first trial. The research team, ______, refined their methodology and repeated the protocol.
options: therefore
however
nevertheless
instead
questions.explanation: 'Therefore' logically links the inconclusive initial outcome to the researchers' rational response of refining and repeating the experiment.

questions.text: Some desert plants store water in thick fleshy stems. Other desert flora, ______, develop extensive root systems to reach deep groundwater.
options: by comparison
in conclusion
for instance
as a result
questions.explanation: 'By comparison' highlights the alternative survival strategy used by other desert flora.

questions.text: The hike to the summit was steep and exhausting. The panoramic view from the peak, ______, made every step worthwhile.
options: however
furthermore
similarly
therefore
questions.explanation: 'However' contrasts the fatigue of the difficult climb with the rewarding beauty of the final summit view.

questions.text: Volunteering at the animal shelter requires a weekly commitment. ______, volunteers must complete a mandatory orientation workshop.
options: Additionally
Consequently
Otherwise
Instead
questions.explanation: 'Additionally' introduces another prerequisite requirement for prospective volunteers.

questions.text: The city council voted against the proposed shopping mall. ______, they approved funds to create a municipal nature preserve on the property.
options: Instead
Therefore
Likewise
For example
questions.explanation: 'Instead' signals the alternative zoning decision adopted in place of the rejected shopping mall.

questions.text: Proper hydration enhances athletic endurance. ______, it facilitates muscle recovery and reduces post-workout soreness.
options: Moreover
Regardless
In spite of this
Conversely
questions.explanation: 'Moreover' adds another physiological advantage of proper hydration during athletic training.

questions.text: The archaeological artifacts were extremely fragile. ______, excavators handled them exclusively with specialized tools and padded containers.
options: For this reason
Nevertheless
Conversely
On the other hand
questions.explanation: 'For this reason' directly explains why the excavators exercised such delicate care when handling the fragile artifacts.

questions.text: The violin requires years of dedicated practice to master. ______, the cello demands rigorous physical and technical discipline.
options: Similarly
On the contrary
However
In contrast
questions.explanation: 'Similarly' compares two string instruments that share the requirement of rigorous discipline and long-term practice.

questions.text: In a right triangle, if the side opposite angle θ is 3 and the hypotenuse is 5, what is sin(θ)?
questions.explanation: By definition, sin(θ) = Opposite / Hypotenuse = 3 / 5.

questions.text: In a right triangle with legs of length 5 and 12, what is the value of cos(θ) for the angle adjacent to the leg of length 5?
questions.explanation: Hypotenuse = √(5² + 12²) = √(25 + 144) = √169 = 13. For the angle adjacent to the leg of length 5: cos(θ) = Adjacent / Hypotenuse = 5 / 13.

questions.text: In a right triangle, if opposite side is 8 and adjacent side is 6, what is tan(θ)?
questions.explanation: tan(θ) = Opposite / Adjacent = 8 / 6 = 4 / 3.

questions.text: What is the exact value of sin(30°)?
questions.explanation: In a standard 30°-60°-90° right triangle, the ratio of the side opposite 30° to the hypotenuse is 1 / 2. So sin(30°) = 1/2.

questions.text: What is the exact value of cos(60°)?
What is the value of tan(45°)?
questions.explanation: In a 45°-45°-90° right triangle, both legs are equal in length. tan(45°) = Opposite / Adjacent = 1 / 1 = 1.

questions.text: Which trigonometric identity is true for all values of θ?
options: sin²(θ) + cos²(θ) = 1
sin(θ) + cos(θ) = 1
tan²(θ) + 1 = sin²(θ)
sin(2θ) = 2 sin(θ)
questions.explanation: The Pythagorean trigonometric identity states that for any angle θ, sin²(θ) + cos²(θ) = 1.

questions.text: If sin(θ) = 4/5 and θ is in Quadrant I, what is cos(θ)?
questions.explanation: Using sin²(θ) + cos²(θ) = 1: cos²(θ) = 1 – (4/5)² = 1 – 16/25 = 9/25 => cos(θ) = √(9/25) = 3/5 (positive in Quadrant I).

questions.text: If cos(θ) = 12/13 in a right triangle, what is tan(θ)?
questions.explanation: Opposite side = √(13² – 12²) = √(169 – 144) = √25 = 5. tan(θ) = Opposite / Adjacent = 5 / 12.

questions.text: What is the value of sin(90°)?
options: Undefined
questions.explanation: On the unit circle, at 90° (π/2 radians), the coordinate is (0, 1), so sin(90°) = 1.

questions.text: What is the value of cos(0°)?
options: Undefined
questions.explanation: On the unit circle, at 0° (0 radians), the coordinate is (1, 0), so cos(0°) = 1.

questions.text: Convert 180° to radians.
options: π radians
2π radians
π/2 radians
3π/2 radians
questions.explanation: Radians = Degrees · (π / 180°) = 180° · (π / 180°) = π radians.

questions.text: Convert π/3 radians into degrees.
What is the reciprocal trigonometric function of cos(θ)?
options: sec(θ)
csc(θ)
cot(θ)
tan(θ)
questions.explanation: The secant function is defined as the reciprocal of cosine: sec(θ) = 1 / cos(θ).

questions.text: What is the reciprocal trigonometric function of sin(θ)?
options: csc(θ)
sec(θ)
cot(θ)
cos(θ)
questions.explanation: The cosecant function is defined as the reciprocal of sine: csc(θ) = 1 / sin(θ).

questions.text: If tan(θ) = 3/4 in Quadrant I, what is sec(θ)?
questions.explanation: Opposite = 3, Adjacent = 4, Hypotenuse = √(3² + 4²) = 5. cos(θ) = 4/5 => sec(θ) = 1 / cos(θ) = 5/4.

questions.text: In right triangle ABC with right angle at C, if angle A = 30° and hypotenuse AB = 10, what is the length of side BC opposite to angle A?
What is the exact value of sin(45°)?
questions.explanation: In a 45°-45°-90° right triangle, sin(45°) = 1 / √2 = √2 / 2.

questions.text: In a right triangle, if angle θ = 70° and the adjacent side is 10, which expression represents the length of the opposite side?
questions.explanation: tan(70°) = Opposite / Adjacent = Opposite / 10 => Opposite = 10 tan(70°).

questions.text: What is the value of cos(90°)?
options: Undefined
questions.explanation: On the unit circle, at 90° (0, 1), the x-coordinate is 0, so cos(90°) = 0.

questions.text:
Which version of the sentence is the most concise and effective?

'Due to the fact that it was raining heavily, the outdoor event was cancelled.'
options: Because it was raining heavily, the outdoor event was cancelled.
Due to the fact that it was raining heavily, the outdoor event was cancelled.
Owing to the heavy rain that was falling down, the outdoor event was cancelled.
The outdoor event was cancelled as a direct result of the fact that rain was heavy.
questions.explanation: 'Because' replaces the wordy multi-word phrase 'Due to the fact that' with a single, clear causal conjunction.

questions.text:
Which phrase in the sentence is redundant?

'The student repeated the same experiment again.'
options: 'repeated... again' — 'repeated' already means doing something again
'the student'
'the same experiment'
'experiment'
questions.explanation: 'Repeat' inherently means to perform or say something again, making the addition of 'again' redundant.

questions.text: Which option eliminates the redundancy in: 'The two siblings collaborated together on the project.'?
options: The two siblings collaborated on the project.
The two siblings worked together in collaboration on the project.
Both of the two siblings collaborated together.
The siblings each collaborated together on the project.
questions.explanation: 'Collaborated' by definition means working together, so 'together' is redundant and should be deleted.

questions.text: Which sentence is the least wordy and most direct?
options: This technological innovation is unprecedented.
This technological innovation is new and has not been seen before in earlier times.
This technological innovation is a totally unprecedented new development.
Being new, this technological innovation had never happened in previous history.
questions.explanation: 'Unprecedented' captures the entire meaning of 'new and never seen before' in a single, powerful word.

questions.text:
Identify the redundant phrase in this sentence:

'The round circle was drawn carefully by the architect.'
options: 'round circle' — a circle is by definition always round
'carefully by the architect'
'was drawn'
'The'
questions.explanation: A circle is geometrically defined as round, so the modifier 'round' is redundant.

questions.text: Which option most concisely rewrites: 'At this point in time, the committee has not yet reached a final decision.'?
options: Currently, the committee has not reached a decision.
At this point in time, the committee has not yet reached a decision.
As of now at this current moment, the committee has not decided.
The committee has not yet decided, which is the case at this point in time.
questions.explanation: 'Currently' cleanly replaces the wordy cliches 'At this point in time' and 'As of now at this current moment'.

questions.text:
Which underlined phrase is wordy and should be replaced with a single adverb?

'She spoke [in a loud manner] during the meeting.'
options: 'loudly'
'in a loud manner'
'loud mannered'
'with loudness'
questions.explanation: The single adverb 'loudly' replaces the three-word prepositional phrase 'in a loud manner' with maximum conciseness.

questions.text: Which option best eliminates wordiness in: 'The reason why the bridge was closed was because of the fact that it was structurally unsound.'?
options: The bridge was closed because it was structurally unsound.
The reason the bridge was closed was that it was structurally unsound.
Due to the fact that it was unsafe, the bridge was closed for being unsound.
The bridge's closure happened due to it being structurally unsafe and unsound.
questions.explanation: 'The bridge was closed because it was structurally unsound' eliminates the wordy double-causal construction 'The reason why... was because of the fact that'.

questions.text: Which phrase is NOT redundant?
options: unexpected obstacle
past history
unexpected surprise
future predictions
questions.explanation: Obstacles can be expected or unexpected, so 'unexpected obstacle' is not redundant. In contrast, history is always in the past, surprises are always unexpected, and predictions always concern the future.

questions.text: Select the most concise version of: 'The coach made the decision to cancel the practice for today.'
options: The coach decided to cancel today's practice.
The coach made the decision to cancel today's practice.
The coach's decision was cancellation of today's practice.
For today, the coach made a practice cancellation decision.
questions.explanation: Changing the nominalization 'made the decision' to the active verb 'decided' streamlines the sentence.

questions.text: Which sentence contains a redundancy that should be corrected?
options: The annual salary is paid once per year.
The professor published several books.
They moved to a new city last spring.
Her reaction surprised us.
questions.explanation: 'Annual' already means occurring once per year, making 'once per year' redundant.

questions.text: Which phrase is wordy and can be replaced by the single conjunction 'although'?
options: 'in spite of the fact that'
'on account of'
'due to'
'as well as'
questions.explanation: 'In spite of the fact that' is a six-word wordy phrase that should be replaced by 'although' or 'even though'.

questions.text: Identify the most concise and clear version of: 'She was of the opinion that the movie was boring.'
options: She thought the movie was boring.
She held the personal belief that the movie was boring to watch.
In her opinion, she believed the movie was boring.
The movie, in her opinion and belief, was a boring experience.
questions.explanation: 'She thought' is direct and concise, eliminating the pompous phrasing 'was of the opinion that'.

questions.text: Which sentence is redundant because an absolute adjective is improperly modified?
options: The painting was very unique.
The soup was very hot.
She was very tired after the hike.
The class was very long.
questions.explanation: 'Unique' means one-of-a-kind (an absolute state); something cannot be 'very unique' or 'more unique'.

questions.text: Choose the option that eliminates wordiness: 'In the event that it rains, the game will be postponed.'
options: If it rains, the game will be postponed.
In the event that rain occurs, the game will be postponed.
Should it rain, the game may in that event be postponed.
The game will be postponed in the event of rain occurring.
questions.explanation: 'If it rains' is the most concise and natural conditional clause, replacing 'In the event that it rains'.

questions.text: Which of the following expressions contains a redundancy?
options: All of the below are redundant
old antique
brief summary
close proximity
questions.explanation: Antiques are by definition old, summaries are brief, and proximity means closeness; all three are redundant pairs.

questions.text: Which sentence is wordy and should be revised for conciseness?
options: Due to the fact that he was tired, he went to bed early.
The report is due Friday.
He ran the marathon in four hours.
She borrowed the book from the library.
questions.explanation: 'Due to the fact that he was tired' should be revised to 'Because he was tired' for conciseness.

questions.text: Which rewrite is the most concise for: 'The meeting was for the purpose of discussing the new budget proposal.'?
options: The meeting discussed the new budget proposal.
The meeting was held for purposes of budget discussion.
The meeting's purpose was a budget proposal discussion.
The purpose of the meeting was for new budget proposal discussions.
questions.explanation: 'The meeting discussed the new budget proposal' uses an active verb, cutting out all bureaucratic padding.

questions.text:
Which phrase in the sentence is redundant?

'The free gift came with every purchase over $50.'
options: 'free gift' — gifts are by definition always free
'every purchase'
'over $50'
'came with'
questions.explanation: A gift is by definition free; therefore, 'free gift' is a redundant phrase.

questions.text: Select the most concise revision of: 'He is a person who always arrives at school on time.'
options: He always arrives at school on time.
He is a person that is always on time to school.
Being a person, he always arrives on time at school.
He is someone who is always on time, arriving at school.
questions.explanation: 'He always arrives at school on time' eliminates the useless empty filler 'He is a person who'.
